---
title: glyim CLI Reference
description: Every flag of the glyim compiler driver — emit kinds, backends, optimization, LTO, targets, diagnostics formats, the standard library prelude, and lint levels.
type: reference
sidebar:
  order: 1
---

import { Aside, Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The `glyim` compiler driver (built as `glyim-cli`) compiles a single `.g` source file. This page documents the complete command-line surface, verified against the argument parser in `crates/glyim-cli`.

<Code lang="bash" code={`glyim <INPUT> [FLAGS]`} />

## Arguments and flags

| Argument | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|----------|------|---------|----------|-------------|
| `<INPUT>` | path | — | yes | The `.g` source file to compile. |
| `-o`, `--output <PATH>` | path | derived | no | Write the output artifact to this path. |
| `--emit <KIND>` | enum | `obj` | no | Output artifact kind — see [emit kinds](#emit-kinds). |
| `-O`, `--opt-level <N>` | 0–3 | `0` | no | Optimization level. |
| `--target <TRIPLE>` | string | host default | no | Target triple, for example `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`. Defaults to `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` when unset. |
| `--backend <NAME>` | enum | `llvm` | no | Code generation backend: `llvm` or `bytecode`. |
| `--linker <PATH>` | path | system linker | no | Override the system linker used to link executables. |
| `--link-flags <FLAGS>` | string | none | no | Extra flags passed to the linker. |
| `--lto <KIND>` | enum | `off` | no | Link-time optimization strategy: `off`, `fat`, or `thin`. |
| `--codegen-units <N>` | integer | parallelism | no | Number of codegen units (CGUs) for parallel code generation. Defaults to the available parallelism, capped at 16. |
| `--proc-macro-deps <LIST>` | string | none | no | Comma-separated proc-macro dependency source files, compiled for the host triple to cdylibs and loaded via `dlopen`. |
| `--error-format <FMT>` | enum | `human` | no | Diagnostic format: `human` (miette-rendered) or `json` (one JSON object per diagnostic). |
| `--with-stdlib` | flag | off | no | Prepend the assembled standard library to the input, so `println`, `Vec`, `Option`, `Result`, `String`, `Box`, `Rc`, and `Iterator` resolve without explicit `use` statements. |
| `-A`, `--allow <LINT>` | lint name | none | no | Suppress the named lint. Repeatable. |
| `-W`, `--warn <LINT>` | lint name | none | no | Set the named lint to warning level (the default). Repeatable. `glyim -W help` lists all lints. |
| `-D`, `--deny <LINT>` | lint name | none | no | Promote the named lint to error level, aborting compilation. Repeatable. |
| `-h`, `--help` | flag | — | no | Print help. |
| `-V`, `--version` | flag | — | no | Print version. |

## Emit kinds

| Kind | Output | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `obj` | Native object file | The default. |
| `exec` | Runnable executable | Requires the LLVM backend; the driver links with the system linker. |
| `mir` | MIR dump | Human-readable mid-level IR, useful for debugging lowering. |
| `llvm-ir` | LLVM IR | Textual `.ll` output of the LLVM backend. |
| `asm` | Assembly | Target assembly for the selected `--target`. |
| `cdylib` | Dynamic library | Used for proc-macro crates; compiled for the host when driven by `--proc-macro-deps`. |

## LTO behavior

| Value | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| `off` | No link-time optimization (default). |
| `fat` | In-compiler module merge and optimize. Requires multi-CGU support, which is not yet implemented; requesting it with multiple CGUs errors cleanly rather than silently ignoring the request. |
| `thin` | Requires the LLVM backend and the `llvm-lto2` tool from the same LLVM distribution the backend was built against. Requesting `thin` with `--backend bytecode` is an explicit error. |

## Internal compiler errors

When the compiler itself panics, the driver catches the unwind and prints a structured ICE (internal compiler error) report instead of a raw Rust backtrace. The report includes the panic message and a backtrace captured at the panic site. A language-oriented error never appears as an ICE; an ICE is always a compiler bug worth reporting.

## Environment

| Variable | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX` | LLVM 23 installation prefix, required to build the workspace. Homebrew: `$(brew --prefix llvm@23)`; Debian/Ubuntu: `/usr/lib/llvm-23`. |

<Aside type="caution">
The LLVM backend is a hard dependency of the pipeline — there is no feature flag to build without it.
</Aside>

## Examples

<Code lang="bash" code={`# Object file with the LLVM backend (defaults)
glyim input.g -o output.o

# LLVM IR for inspection
glyim input.g --emit llvm-ir

# Optimized executable with thin LTO
glyim input.g --emit exec -O2 --lto thin -o hello

# Cross-compile to AArch64 Linux
glyim input.g --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu

# JSON diagnostics for editor tooling
glyim input.g --error-format json

# Prepend the standard library, deny the unsafe_fn_call lint
glyim input.g --with-stdlib -D unsafe`} />

## Next steps

See [inspect the compilation pipeline](/guides/inspect-compilation/) for task-oriented walkthroughs of these flags, and the [lint reference](/reference/lints/) for the lint framework.


---

---
title: Crate Reference
description: Every crate in the Glyim Cargo workspace and its role in the compilation pipeline.
type: reference
sidebar:
  order: 5
---

import { Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Glyim is organized as a Cargo workspace of small, single-responsibility crates. Each phase consumes the previous phase's IR and exposes a minimal trait-based interface, so tests can substitute mocks for any phase. All crates live under `crates/`.

## Foundation

| Crate | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `glyim-core` | Foundation types: index vectors, definition IDs, interner, paths, ABI constants, the lint registry. |
| `glyim-span` | Source locations (file, byte index, span), hygiene contexts, multispan diagnostics. |
| `glyim-diag` | Diagnostic types, error codes, `DiagSink`, `miette` integration. |
| `glyim-vfs` | Virtual file system with in-memory file content tracking. |
| `glyim-db` | Compilation database: interners, VFS, type context, trait context. |

## Frontend

| Crate | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `glyim-syntax` | CST definition (Rowan-based), `SyntaxKind` enum, AST node helpers, including the `Gsx*` node kinds. |
| `glyim-frontend` | Lexer and parser (merged), produces `SyntaxNode`. The parser handles GSX elements with zero lexer changes. |
| `glyim-meta` | Macro expansion: `macro_rules!` declarative macros and built-in macros. |
| `glyim-proc-macro` | C-compatible proc-macro ABI, registry, and `dlopen` loader. |

## Analysis

| Crate | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `glyim-def-map` | Module graph, item scopes, name resolution. |
| `glyim-hir` | High-level IR (untyped), lowered from the CST. Preserves GSX element structure. |
| `glyim-type` | Type interning (`TyCtx`), type kinds, substitutions, regions, predicates, auto-traits, object safety, layout hints, printing. |
| `glyim-solve` | `InferenceTable`, unification, trait solver, fulfillment context, HRTB support. |
| `glyim-typeck` | Type checker: HIR to THIR with inference and trait resolution, including `check_gsx`. |
| `glyim-const-eval` | Constant expression evaluator over HIR. |

## Lowering and MIR

| Crate | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `glyim-mir` | Mid-level IR (CFG), place types, statement and terminator kinds. |
| `glyim-lower` | THIR to MIR lowering, monomorphization, CGU partitioning, polymorphization, post-mono lint checks. |
| `glyim-borrowck` | NLL borrow checker with two-phase borrows, move analysis, and drop-flag elaboration. |
| `glyim-opt` | MIR optimization passes: constant propagation, DCE, CFG simplification, unreachable block elimination, slice desugaring, drop elaboration. |
| `glyim-mir-interp` | Interpreter for MIR, used for `const fn` evaluation and test execution. |

## Code generation and runtime

| Crate | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `glyim-layout` | Type layout computation (size, alignment, ABI, vtables) with ABI-aware argument passing (`sret`, `byval`, `Ignore`, `Direct`, `Split`). |
| `glyim-codegen` | Abstract code generation backend trait plus the bytecode backend. |
| `glyim-codegen-llvm` | LLVM backend (via `inkwell`, LLVM 23) with full ABI handling, debug info, exception handling, and LTO. |
| `glyim-bytecode-vm` | Switch-dispatch VM executing the bytecode backend's output. |
| `glyim-runtime` | Runtime FFI: alloc, dealloc, drop glue, panic, fs/net/thread/time/process. |

## GSX

| Crate | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `glyim-gsx` | View IR (skeleton, slots, regions), flat-`u32` blueprints, read/write-set analysis, mutation-specialized patches, SSR emitter, `Host` trait and headless test host, keyed-list LIS reconciliation. |

## Tooling

| Crate | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `glyim-pipeline` | End-to-end compilation driver: lex, parse, def-map, HIR, typeck, lower, borrowck, opt, codegen. |
| `glyim-cli` | Command-line interface (`clap`) and linker driver. Built as `glyim-cli`. |
| `glyim-lsp` | Language Server Protocol implementation: diagnostics, hover, completion, navigation, code actions. |
| `glyim-test` | Testing framework: discovery, five test modes, snapshots, mocks, property testing. |
| `glyip` | Package manager and build tool. |

## Standard library source

| Crate | Contents |
|-------|----------|
| `glyim-lang-core` | Core library source (`.g` files): `Option`, `Result`, `iter`, `slice`, `str`, `cell`, `mem`, `ptr`, `ops`, `cmp`, `marker`, `panic`, `hint`, `convert`, `default`, `future`. |
| `glyim-lang-alloc` | Allocation library source: `Box`, `Vec`, `String`, `Rc`, `RawVec`. |
| `glyim-lang-std` | Standard library source: `io`, `fs`, `net`, `thread`, `sync`, `env`, `time`, `process`, `task`. |

<Aside type="note">
The standard library is written in Glyim and consumed by the compiler as its bootstrapping corpus. The compiler itself is Rust — Glyim is not yet self-hosting.
</Aside>

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Architecture, explained" href="/explanation/architecture/" description="Why the workspace is split this way: context traits, arena IRs, and interning." />
<LinkCard title="The pipeline, explained" href="/explanation/pipeline/" description="How the crates connect from source.g to a native binary." />


---

---
title: glyip Reference
description: The glyip build tool commands and the complete Glyip.toml manifest schema — package metadata, targets, and dependency declarations.
type: reference
sidebar:
  order: 2
---

import { Aside, Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`glyip` is Cargo's counterpart for Glyim projects. It reads a `Glyip.toml` manifest, resolves dependencies with SemVer 2.0 matching, maintains a `Glyip.lock` lockfile, and drives the compiler.

## Commands

### `glyip new`

Scaffold a new project.

| Argument / flag | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------------|------|---------|-------------|
| `<NAME>` | string | — | Project name. |
| `--lib` | flag | off | Create a library project instead of a binary. |
| `--edition <EDITION>` | string | `2024` | Language edition. |

<Code lang="bash" code={`glyip new my_project
glyip new my_lib --lib`} />

### `glyip build`

Compile the project. Builds are incremental — sources and build configuration are fingerprinted with SHA-256.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--release` | flag | off | Build in release mode. |
| `--target <TRIPLE>` | string | host | Target triple. |
| `--backend <NAME>` | `llvm` \| `bytecode` | `llvm` | Codegen backend. `bytecode` output is not directly runnable. |
| `--opt-level <N>` | 0–3 | `0` | Optimization level. |
| `--lto <KIND>` | `off` \| `thin` \| `fat` | `off` | Link-time optimization. Unknown values are treated as `off`. |

<Code lang="bash" code={`glyip build --release -O2`} />

### `glyip test`

Run the project's tests.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--release` | flag | off | Build in release mode. |
| `--filter <SUBSTRING>` | string | all | Run only tests whose name contains the substring. |
| `--no-run` | flag | off | Compile the tests but do not run them. |
| `--compiled` | flag | off | Compile each test file to a native executable and run it as a real subprocess instead of the in-process MIR interpreter. |

<Code lang="bash" code={`glyip test --filter parser --compiled`} />

### `glyip run`

Build and execute the project's binary. Always uses the LLVM backend, because running requires an executable the operating system can start. Exits with the child's exit status.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--release` | flag | off | Build in release mode. |
| `--target <TRIPLE>` | string | host | Target triple. |
| `--lto <KIND>` | `off` \| `thin` \| `fat` | `off` | Link-time optimization. |
| `-- <ARGS>` | strings | none | Everything after `--` is passed to the program. |

<Code lang="bash" code={`glyip run -- --flag value`} />

## The `Glyip.toml` manifest

The manifest is parsed with unknown-key rejection: an unrecognized key is an error.

### `[package]`

| Key | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-----|------|---------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | string | — | yes | Crate name. |
| `version` | string | `"0.1.0"` | no | Semantic version. |
| `edition` | string | `"2024"` | no | Language edition. |
| `authors` | string array | `[]` | no | Author list. |
| `description` | string | none | no | Short description. |
| `bin` | table array | none | no | Binary targets. |
| `lib` | table | none | no | Library target. |

Each `bin` entry accepts `name` (required) and `path` (source file, relative to the project root). The `lib` entry accepts `path`.

### `[dependencies]` and `[dev-dependencies]`

Both sections map a crate name to either a bare version requirement or a detail table:

<Code lang="toml" code={`[dependencies]
serde = "1.0"
local_util = { path = "../local_util" }
my_crate = { git = "https://github.com/example/my_crate", tag = "v0.3.0" }

[dev-dependencies]
test_helpers = { path = "../test_helpers" }`} />

| Key | Type | Description |
|-----|------|-------------|
| `version` | string | SemVer 2.0 requirement — caret, tilde, wildcard, and comparison operators are supported. |
| `path` | path | Local filesystem dependency. |
| `git` | URL | Git repository dependency. |
| `branch` | string | Track a named branch (resolved to its current tip commit). |
| `tag` | string | Track a named tag (resolved to the commit the tag points at). |
| `rev` | string | Pin an exact revision hash. |

Exactly one git ref is active; without `branch`, `tag`, or `rev`, the repository's default branch tip is used.

### The lockfile

`glyip` maintains `Glyip.lock` with entries keyed by `name-version`, so repeated builds resolve the same graph. The conflict check enforces one resolved version per crate name — see [manage dependencies](/guides/manage-dependencies/) for the resolver's exact semantics.

<Aside type="tip">
A typo in a version string is an error (`DependencyNotFound`), not a silent fallback to the latest version.
</Aside>

## Next steps

See [manage dependencies](/guides/manage-dependencies/) for practical workflows, and [test your code](/guides/test-your-code/) for testing patterns.


---

---
title: GSX Reference
description: The GSX view syntax and the glyim-gsx compiler stage API — grammar, directives, regions, blueprints, hosts, and diagnostics.
type: reference
sidebar:
  order: 6
---

import { Aside, Badge, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

GSX is Glyim's first-class, typed, host-agnostic view syntax: JSX's ergonomics, but a compiler-visible structure instead of a runtime function-call tree. Elements are data described by schemas, and the same source can target HTML, SSR strings, native widgets, terminals, and headless test hosts.

<Aside type="caution">
GSX is experimental <Badge text="v0.1" variant="note" />. The parsing, type checking, and the `glyim-gsx` stage are implemented and tested, but the CLI driver does not run the GSX stage yet — see the [authoring guide](/guides/write-gsx-views/) for the current usage path.
</Aside>

## Grammar

| Construct | Syntax | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Element | `<tag attrs> children </tag>` or `<tag attrs />` | Prefix-position `<` followed by an identifier. Lowercase tags resolve through the active dialect schema; uppercase tags resolve through the def-map as components. |
| Fragment | `<> … </>` | Grouping without a host element. |
| Text | `"Hello"`, `"Hello {name}"` | Always a string literal — there is no raw-text mode, so the lexer is unchanged. The parser splits the literal into static pieces and typed holes at parse time. |
| Dynamic child | `{expr}` | Any expression of type `View` or a text-able type. |
| Attribute | `name="lit"`, `name={expr}` | Static string or dynamic expression. |
| Bare attribute | `disabled` | Equivalent to `disabled={true}`. |
| Shorthand | `{name}` | Equivalent to `name={name}`. |
| Spread | `{..props}` | Typed against the target's prop struct. |
| Event directive | `on:click={handler}` | Handlers are state transformers `fn(&mut S, E)`, not capturing closures. |
| Class directive | `class:active={cond}` | Statically decomposed into slots. |
| Style directive | `style:width={px}` | Statically decomposed into slots. |
| Two-way binding | `bind:value={place}` | `place` is a place expression (lvalue); desugared with echo suppression. |
| Control flow | `if`, `match`, `for` inside `{ }` | The language is the template language. The compiler recognizes these forms as regions. |
| Keyed iteration | `for x in xs by key { … }` | `by` is a GSX-scoped contextual keyword, accepted only in child-position `for`. |
| Namespaced dialect | `<web:canvas/>`, `<native:window/>` | Escape hatch for host-specific elements. |
| Macro escape hatch | `gsx! { … }` | Optional token-tree entry for use inside macros. |

Hyphenated attribute and tag names (such as `aria-label`) are accepted.

## The compilation model

A GSX expression travels through the pipeline as structure, never as a desugared call tree:

1. **CST** — dedicated `Gsx*` node kinds (`GsxElement`, `GsxFragment`, `GsxDirectiveAttr`, `GsxSpread`, `GsxTextLit`, `GsxBlockChild`, `GsxForBy`, …) parsed by `parse_gsx_element` with zero lexer changes.
2. **HIR** — `Expr::Gsx` preserves the element structure.
3. **Typeck** — `check_gsx` validates tags, props, events, and children against the active dialect schema and checks every hole expression.
4. **The `glyim-gsx` stage** — where views become programs:
   - **VIR** (View IR): static skeleton, dynamic slots, and regions (`if`, `match`, keyed `for`, component).
   - **Analyses**: read-sets and write-sets per slot, with prefix interference detection.
   - **MSPs** (mutation-specialized patches): one straight-line patch function per distinct write-set.
   - **Emit**: a `Blueprint` — a flat `u32` operation array plus a string table — and an SSR string emitter.

## Public API surface (`glyim-gsx`)

| Item | Role |
|------|------|
| Schema / Dialect registry | Describes tags, props, events, and children per host dialect; the compiler validates against schemas, never against tag-name strings. |
| `Host` trait | The interface a rendering backend implements: mount, patch, patch-mask, dispatch, SSR. |
| Headless host | An op-recording `Host` implementation for tests; assertions state exact update costs. |
| `ViewRuntime::mount` | Mounts a blueprint onto a host and returns a live view handle. |
| Blueprint | Flat-`u32` ops plus string table; encodable as a static for AOT embedding. |
| SSR emitter | Renders a blueprint to an HTML-like string server-side. |
| Keyed-list reconciliation | Longest-increasing-subsequence algorithm for `for … by` lists. |

## Diagnostics

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `G0201` | A value cannot be tracked by ownership analysis and needs the `Signal<T>` escape hatch; the diagnostic ships a fix-it, and the host falls back to signal bits for that slot. |
| hand-off diagnostic | A GSX-containing body reached the end of typeck without the GSX stage running — a clean pointer to the stage API, not an internal error. |

## Status and scope :badge[experimental]{variant="caution"}

- Implemented and tested: syntax, HIR preservation, schema-driven typeck, VIR, analyses, MSPs, blueprint + SSR emission, keyed reconciliation, `bind:` desugaring with echo suppression, composition as lens composition for inlined components, the §3.1 Counter example end to end (flagship tests in `crates/glyim-gsx/tests/counter.rs`).
- Not started: host dialect `.g` libraries (`glyim-lang-ui`), arena node trees, layout, styles, accessibility-tree emission, a WASM host protocol, a VM-based hot-reload host, and CLI driver wiring.

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Write GSX views" href="/guides/write-gsx-views/" description="A task-oriented walkthrough with the flagship Counter example." />
<LinkCard title="Ownership-driven reactivity" href="/explanation/gsx-reactivity/" description="Why mutation-specialized patches replace vdom diffing." />


---

---
title: Language Reference
description: The Glyim language — declarations, types, traits, pattern matching, closures, async/await, macros, and compiler-known builtin types.
type: reference
sidebar:
  order: 3
---

import { Aside, Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Glyim is a Rust-like systems programming language with its own file extension, `.g`. This page lists the constructs the compiler accepts. The full grammar is still evolving — the `glyim-lang-core`, `glyim-lang-alloc`, and `glyim-lang-std` crates contain the current standard library source, written in Glyim, and serve as the compiler's bootstrapping corpus.

## A tour in one block

<Code lang="rust" code={`// Structs, enums, generics, traits.
struct Point<T> {
    x: T,
    y: T,
}

enum Shape {
    Circle(f64),
    Rectangle(f64, f64),
    Point,
}

trait Area {
    fn area(&self) -> f64;
}

impl Area for Shape {
    fn area(&self) -> f64 {
        match self {
            Shape::Circle(r) => 3.14159 * r * r,
            Shape::Rectangle(w, h) => w * h,
            Shape::Point => 0.0,
        }
    }
}

// Pattern matching, ranges, guards.
fn classify(n: i32) -> &str {
    match n {
        0 => "zero",
        1 | 2 => "small",
        x if x < 0 => "negative",
        _ => "large",
    }
}

// Closures and iterators.
fn sum_of_squares(values: &[i32]) -> i32 {
    values.iter().map(|x| *x * *x).sum()
}

// Async / await.
async fn fetch_twice() -> i32 {
    let a = fetch_one().await;
    let b = fetch_one().await;
    a + b
}`} />

## Constructs

### Declarations

| Construct | Syntax | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Function | `fn name(params) -> Ret { … }` | Free functions and associated functions in `impl` blocks. |
| Struct | `struct Name { field: T, … }` | Tuple and unit forms supported. Generic parameters with bounds and where-clauses. |
| Enum | `enum Name { A, B(T), C { x: T } }` | Algebraic data types. |
| Trait | `trait Name { fn method(&self); }` | Default methods and associated types are supported. |
| Impl | `impl Trait for Type { … }` / `impl Type { … }` | Static dispatch through the trait system. |
| Local binding | `let pattern: Type = expr;` | Types are usually inferred. |

### Control flow

| Construct | Forms |
|-----------|-------|
| Conditional | `if expr { … } else { … }` |
| Loop | `while cond { … }`, `loop { … }`, `for x in iter { … }` |
| Match | `match expr { pattern => arm, … }` |
| Async | `async fn …` and `expr.await` — desugared to state machines (straight-line and multi-await bodies). |

### Pattern matching

Patterns support literals, ranges, or-patterns (`1 | 2`), slices, structs, tuples, enums, bindings, and `if` guards. The wildcard `_` covers unmatched cases. Match arms are checked for exhaustiveness by the type checker.

### Generics and traits

- Type parameters: `struct Point<T>`, `fn f<T: Trait>(…)`, and where-clauses.
- Trait bounds participate in the trait solver, which handles higher-ranked trait bounds (`for<'a>`).
- Auto-traits (`Send`, `Sync`, `Unpin`) are computed automatically.
- Trait objects use vtable generation for dynamic dispatch.

### Closures

Closures capture their environment with capture analysis that classifies each capture as `ByValue`, `ByRef(Mut)`, or `ByRef(Not)`. Closure syntax mirrors Rust: `|x| x + 1`, `|x: i32| -> i32 { x + 1 }`.

### Unsafe

`unsafe fn` declares a function with unchecked contracts. Calls to an `unsafe fn` outside an enclosing `unsafe { }` block trigger the [`unsafe_fn_call` lint](/reference/lints/), which warns by default and can be allowed or denied from the CLI.

### Macros

Declarative macros use `macro_rules!` with fragment specifiers including `:expr`, `:ty`, `:pat`, and `:tt`. Built-in macros:

| Macro | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `file!`, `line!`, `column!` | Source location reporting. |
| `env!`, `option_env!` | Environment variable access (required / optional). |
| `include!`, `include_str!`, `include_bytes!` | Embed other files at compile time. |
| `concat!`, `concat_idents!` | Literal and identifier concatenation. |
| `stringify!` | Render an expression as a string literal. |

Procedural macros are supported through a C-compatible token-stream ABI (`glyim-proc-macro`) with a `dlopen`-based cdylib loader, driven by the `--proc-macro-deps` CLI flag.

### Compiler-known builtin types

| Category | Types |
|----------|-------|
| Primitives | `i32`, `u32`, `f64`, `bool`, `char`, `str`, `&str` and friends |
| Ranges | `Range`, `RangeInclusive`, and the `..` / `..=` syntax |
| Optional / fallible | `Option<T>`, `Result<T, E>` |
| Collections | `Vec<T>`, `String` |
| Smart pointers | `Box<T>`, `Rc`, `PhantomData<T>`, `UnsafeCell<T>` |

<Aside type="note">
Some builtin methods on `Vec`, `String`, `Result`, and `Option` lower to synthetic function bodies that the LLVM backend must intrinsic-lower; unimplemented ones produce an explicit compiler error rather than wrong code.
</Aside>

## Standard library

The standard library is written in Glyim and ships in three crates:

- **`glyim-lang-core`** — `Option`, `Result`, `iter`, `slice`, `str`, `cell`, `mem`, `ptr`, `ops`, `cmp`, `marker`, `panic`, `hint`, `convert`, `default`, `future`.
- **`glyim-lang-alloc`** — `Box`, `Vec`, `String`, `Rc`, `RawVec`.
- **`glyim-lang-std`** — `io`, `fs`, `net`, `thread`, `sync`, `env`, `time`, `process`, `task`.

Pass [`--with-stdlib`](/reference/cli/) to the compiler (or use `glyip`, which does this for you) to make these names resolve without explicit `use` statements.

## Next steps

See the [GSX reference](/reference/gsx/) for view syntax, and [the pipeline explained](/explanation/pipeline/) for how the compiler processes these constructs.


---

---
title: Lint Reference
description: The compiler lint framework — available lints, their aliases, severity levels, and the -A/-W/-D command-line flags.
type: reference
sidebar:
  order: 4
---

import { Aside, Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The compiler's lint framework (§3.5.30 in the internal plan) assigns a severity level to named checks. This page documents every available lint and the flags that control them.

## Lints

| Lint | Alias | Default level | Fires when |
|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| `unsafe_fn_call` | `unsafe` | warn | A declared `unsafe fn` is called outside any enclosing `unsafe { }` block. |
| `unused_generic_params` | `unused_generics` | warn | A monomorphized function does not use one or more of its generic parameters. Checked post-monomorphization by `glyim-lower`. |

The lint list is small by design and grows deliberately: adding a lint means adding a variant, a canonical name, the check that emits the diagnostic, and a drift-detection test so the lint cannot become invisible to `-W help`.

## Levels

| Level | Flag | Behavior |
|-------|------|----------|
| allow | `-A`, `--allow` | Suppress the diagnostic entirely. |
| warn | `-W`, `--warn` | Emit as a warning. This is the default. |
| deny | `-D`, `--deny` | Emit as an error and abort compilation at the pipeline's error gate. |

All three flags are repeatable, and later flags override earlier ones for the same lint.

## Usage

<Code lang="bash" code={`# Promote the unsafe_fn_call lint to an error
glyim input.g -D unsafe

# Suppress it
glyim input.g -A unsafe_fn_call

# Explicitly set warning level
glyim input.g -W unused_generic_params

# List every available lint name and alias
glyim -W help`} />

`glyim -W help` answers before argument parsing enforces the required input file, so it works as a standalone command.

<Aside type="caution">
Unknown lint names are currently ignored silently by the flag parser. Attribute-based control (`#[allow(..)]` and friends) is not yet implemented; levels are set from the command line only.
</Aside>

## Next steps

See the [CLI reference](/reference/cli/) for the full flag table, and the [language reference](/reference/language/#unsafe) for `unsafe fn` semantics.


---

---
title: Getting Started with Glyim
description: Build the Glyim compiler from source, scaffold a project with glyip, and run your first Glyim program end to end.
type: tutorial
sidebar:
  order: 1
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard, Steps, TabItem, Tabs } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

In this tutorial you build the Glyim compiler from source, create a new project with the `glyip` build tool, and run a Glyim program. You finish with a working toolchain and a mental model of the build workflow.

## Prerequisites

- **Rust** — latest stable toolchain, 2024 edition. Rust 1.94 or newer is recommended; the declared MSRV is 1.85.
- **LLVM 23** — required by the LLVM backend. The backend is a hard dependency of the workspace; there is no feature flag to build without it.
- **`just`** and **`watchexec`** — optional, only for the convenience recipes in the repository's `justfile`.

Before building, set `LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX` to your LLVM 23 installation prefix:

<Tabs>
   <TabItem label="macOS (Homebrew)">
        <Code lang="bash" code={`export LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX="$(brew --prefix llvm@23)"`} />
   </TabItem>
   <TabItem label="Debian / Ubuntu">
        <Code lang="bash" code={`export LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX="/usr/lib/llvm-23"`} />
   </TabItem>
</Tabs>

<Aside type="tip">
Add the `export` line to your shell profile so every future session picks it up. The CI pipeline installs LLVM 23 with the `llvm.sh 23` script if you need a reproducible reference setup.
</Aside>

## Build the compiler

<Steps>

1. Clone the repository:

   <Code lang="bash" code={`git clone https://github.com/elcoosp/glyim
cd glyim`} />

2. Build the workspace in release mode:

   <Code lang="bash" code={`cargo build --release`} />

3. Locate the compiler driver. The binary is at `target/release/glyim-cli` — invoke it as `glyim-cli` (rename or symlink it to `glyim` if you prefer):

   <Code lang="bash" code={`./target/release/glyim-cli --version`} />

   You can also invoke the driver through Cargo on every call, which avoids symlinks:

   <Code lang="bash" code={`cargo run -p glyim-cli -- --help`} />

</Steps>

## Create and run a project

`glyip` is Cargo's counterpart for Glyim projects. It reads a `Glyip.toml` manifest, resolves dependencies, maintains a `Glyip.lock` lockfile, and drives the compiler.

<Steps>

1. Scaffold a new binary project:

   <Code lang="bash" code={`cargo run -p glyip -- new hello
cd hello`} />

2. Inspect what `glyip new` generated. The project contains a `Glyip.toml` manifest and a `src/main.g` source file:

   <Code lang="bash" code={`cat Glyip.toml
cat src/main.g`} />

3. Build the project:

   <Code lang="bash" code={`cargo run -p glyip -- build`} />

4. Run it:

   <Code lang="bash" code={`cargo run -p glyip -- run`} />

   `glyip run` is a transparent wrapper: it exits with the compiled program's exit code, so a failing program does not look like a passing command.

</Steps>

## What the scaffold looks like

The scaffolded manifest declares the package and its targets:

<Code lang="toml" code={`[package]
name = "hello"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"`} />

The default template produces a binary that prints a greeting. Edit `src/main.g`, rebuild, and run again — `glyip build` uses SHA-256 source fingerprints, so it recompiles only what changed.

## Compile a single file directly

Once you are comfortable with `glyip`, you can bypass project management and drive the compiler directly. The equivalent of the tutorial so far, in one command:

<Code lang="bash" code={`glyim-cli src/main.g --emit exec -o hello
./hello`} />

The `--emit exec` flag produces a runnable executable; the default `--emit obj` produces an object file. See the [CLI reference](/reference/cli/) for every flag.

## Next steps

You have a working toolchain. From here:

<LinkCard title="Build and run your project" href="/guides/build-and-run/" description="Release builds, optimization levels, LTO, and passing arguments to your program." />
<LinkCard title="Manage dependencies" href="/guides/manage-dependencies/" description="Path, registry, and git dependencies in Glyip.toml, and how the resolver behaves." />
<LinkCard title="How the pipeline works" href="/explanation/pipeline/" description="A stage-by-stage walkthrough of what happens between source.g and a native binary." />
